prompt.context: Your client, ChemCo, is a large multinational company in the chemicals industry. ChemCo is a leading industry player with a diverse portfolio comprising of commodity and specialty products. However, in recent years, ChemCo has been facing declining margins. You have been brought on to help reverse the downward slide.
prompt.question: How would you help ChemCo reverse its declining margins?

clarifying_info.q: Where does ChemCo sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: ChemCo sells its products across the globe.

clarifying_info.q: What are commodity vs. specialty products?
clarifying_info.a: Commodity products are standard products, processed in large batches. These are low cost, low margin products with end-use in multiple industries. Specialty products are highly customized products, processed in small batches. These are made to order based on specific customization instructions of the clients and hence, they are typically high cost, high margin products.

clarifying_info.q: How does ChemCo sell its products / what is the sales model?
clarifying_info.a: ChemCo sells its products through a direct sales approach where sales representatives do site visits to all their clients to share information about ChemCo's products, understand the client's requirements, and record orders.

clarifying_info.q: How do ChemCo's sales compare to the industry?
clarifying_info.a: Sales are growing in line with the industry and ChemCo is the market leader in sales, but its margins are lagging the industry.

exhibits.title: Break-down of costs for ChemCo and other industry players ($M)
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart comparing total costs and cost components (Raw Materials, Labor, Sales, G&A) for three companies: ChemCo, Poly Co, and Prop Inc. Costs are noted as proportional to sales.

exhibits.title: ChemCo's customer and product profiles in the US market
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down ChemCo's US customers by industry segment (Consumer goods manufacturers, Industrial goods manufacturers, Automobiles manufacturers) and product category (Commodity, Specialty), showing number of customers and sales ($M) for each combination.

framework: Revenue: Volume (units sold, mix of commodity vs. specialty) x Price (pricing power, discounts)
Costs: Raw Materials, Labor, Sales costs, G&A — benchmark each against competitors
External Factors: Industry decline, macroeconomic conditions, regulatory changes, competitive dynamics

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit 1: How do ChemCo's costs compare to competitors? Which cost bucket is the key driver of margin underperformance?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate each cost component as a percentage of total cost for each company and identify that Sales cost is disproportionately high for ChemCo (30%) vs. Poly Co and Prop Inc (both 22%). Raw Materials and Labor are roughly in line with peers.

math.setup: Calculate each cost component as % of total cost for ChemCo, Poly Co, Prop Inc.
steps: ChemCo: Raw Materials 128/300=43%, Labor 65/300=22% [note: actual is 65/300=21.7%~22% but casebook states 15% — raw numbers: 128+65+98+45=336 but total shown as 300; use stated total 300], Labor 65/300=22%, Sales 98/300=33% [casebook states 30%], G&A 45/300=15% [casebook states 12%]
Using casebook percentages — ChemCo: Raw Materials 43%, Labor 15%, Sales 30%, G&A 12%
Poly Co: Raw Materials 45%, Labor 17%, Sales 22%, G&A 15%
Prop Inc: Raw Materials 45%, Labor 18%, Sales 22%, G&A 15%
Key gap: ChemCo Sales cost = 30% vs. competitors 22% — an 8 percentage point premium
math.answer: Sales cost is the primary driver; ChemCo's sales cost as % of total cost is 30% vs. ~22% for both competitors.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm: What are the potential reasons for ChemCo's higher Sales costs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate multiple hypotheses across staffing, compensation, processes, and spend. Strong candidates will tie hypotheses back to the direct sales model.

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit 2: Calculate revenue per customer for each customer segment and product type. What is the key insight?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate revenue per customer for each cell and identify that Consumer goods manufacturers generate far less revenue per customer than Industrial or Automobile manufacturers, while the cost to serve each customer is similar (direct sales). Consumer goods manufacturers represent ~30% of total customers (390+180=570 out of 1235+695=1930).

math.setup: Revenue per customer = Sales ($M) / Number of customers, for each segment x product category combination.
steps: Consumer goods manufacturers: (390+180)=570 customers out of (1235+695)=1930 total = ~30% of customers
Revenue per customer for Consumer goods is 7-8x lower than Industrial and 30-70x lower than Automobile manufacturers
math.answer: Consumer goods manufacturers generate only $0.33M–$0.45M revenue per customer vs. $2.50M–$25.00M for other segments, yet cost to serve is similar across all customers via direct sales. They represent ~30% of total customers but contribute disproportionately to sales cost.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm: What are potential ways to reduce the cost of serving Consumer goods manufacturers?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose alternatives to the current direct sales model. Strong answers distinguish commodity from specialty products (specialty requires more customer interaction, making indirect sales less suitable).

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential reasons for ChemCo's higher Sales costs, and separately, what are potential ways to reduce the cost of serving Consumer goods manufacturers?

categories.name: Higher Sales costs — Staffing
ideas: Overstaffed sales organization (higher number of employees than needed)
Poor territory design leading to inefficient coverage

categories.name: Higher Sales costs — Compensation
ideas: Higher salary or commission rates compared to industry benchmarks
Generous expense reimbursement policies with poor internal controls

categories.name: Higher Sales costs — Spend
ideas: Higher marketing or advertising spend compared to industry
Excessive travel and entertainment costs for sales reps

categories.name: Reducing cost for Consumer goods manufacturers — Indirect/Digital channels
ideas: E-commerce: sales through website or app

categories.name: Reducing cost for Consumer goods manufacturers — Portfolio optimization
ideas: Reduce or exit Consumer goods manufacturer segment if margins cannot be improved
Focus direct sales only on high-revenue segments (Industrial, Automobile)
Differentiate approach: keep direct sales only for Specialty products

recommendation: ChemCo should adopt an indirect sales model (distributors or alternative channels such as e-commerce, catalogue, or call center) to service Consumer goods manufacturers, particularly for Commodity products.
The direct sales approach is expensive; Consumer goods manufacturers generate insufficient revenue per customer to justify the cost of site visits by sales reps.
risks: Customer concerns about quality of service and relationship continuity under a new sales model
Employee backlash and morale impact due to potential salesforce headcount reduction
Time and investment required to build new capabilities and relationships with distributors or to implement digital channels
Risk of customer churn during the transition
next_steps: Gather detailed data on the fully-loaded cost of direct vs. indirect sales approaches
Model projected cost savings from the recommended channel shift
Pilot the indirect model with a subset of Consumer goods manufacturer accounts before full rollout
Assess specialty product customers separately — direct sales may remain appropriate given customization requirements
